note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in NJ.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Bayshore Heritage Scenic Byway
byways.designation: New Jersey Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Salem, Cumberland and Cape May counties: CR 540 in Mannington Township via Salem, Greenwich, Bridgeton, Port Norris and Heislerville to Cape May Point State Park; 122-mile spine, 142 miles with spurs

facts.fact: Runs along the Delaware Bay from Mannington Township in Salem County to Cape May Point State Park; main spine 122 miles, 142 with spurs to Fort Mott, East Point Lighthouse, the Cape May-Lewes Ferry and Sunset Beach.

The bay shore is largely wetlands, salt marsh and mud flats and holds the largest population of spawning horseshoe crabs in the world; Bayshore towns lived on oystering, shipbuilding, glass making and salt hay farming.
East Point Light at the mouth of the Maurice River was built in 1849 and is the second oldest lighthouse in New Jersey.
Listed by FHWA as a National Scenic Byway.

byways.review: Catalog lists it only as a state byway; FHWA now lists it as a National Scenic Byway (FHWA byway id 81510).

byways.name: Delaware River Scenic Byway
byways.designation: New Jersey Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: NJ 29 from the Route 29 tunnel in Trenton to the Uhlerstown-Frenchtown Bridge in Frenchtown, Mercer and Hunterdon counties, about 34 miles

facts.fact: Route 29 from the tunnel in Trenton to the Uhlerstown-Frenchtown Bridge, with the Delaware River and the Delaware and Raritan Feeder Canal in view for much of the drive, through Titusville, Lambertville, Stockton, Raven Rock and Frenchtown.

It was the first New Jersey Scenic Byway, designated in 1996, and was nationally designated in 2009; Bull's Island is reached from Pennsylvania by a steel suspension footbridge and the Prallsville Mills stand in Stockton.
Prallsville lies on Route 29 by Stockton where Wickecheoke Creek meets the Delaware; the Prallsville district was listed on the National Register in 1979.

byways.name: Millstone Valley Scenic Byway
byways.designation: New Jersey Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Canal Road and River Road loop between Kingston and Millstone/Manville, mostly Somerset County with parts of Mercer and Middlesex, 25 to 27.5 miles

facts.fact: The Delaware and Raritan Canal runs through most of the byway with Canal Road on one side and River Road on the other; the land between is Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park.
State designation came in 2001 and national designation in 2009; the route passes through eleven National Register historic districts including Kingston, Rocky Hill, Griggstown and East Millstone.
The byway visitor center is in one of the original D&R Canal bridgetender's houses at 2 Griggstown Causeway, open weekend afternoons from April through October.

byways.review: NJDOT gives the length as 25 miles in its text and about 27.5 miles in its fact box.

byways.name: Palisades Scenic Byway
byways.designation: New Jersey Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Palisades Interstate Parkway (10.6 mi) and Henry Hudson Drive (8.5 mi), Fort Lee at the George Washington Bridge to the New York line in Alpine, Bergen County

facts.fact: The byway is the Palisades Interstate Parkway on top of the cliffs and Henry Hudson Drive below it by the river, from the George Washington Bridge to the New York line at Alpine; State Line Lookout sits at the highest point of the cliffs, 532 feet. State designation 2005.

Henry Hudson Drive was built between 1912 and 1940 and runs about 8 miles along the river from the Edgewater entrance to Alpine, past Ross Dock and the Englewood and Undercliff picnic areas; part of it closes to cars December to April.
Listed by FHWA as a National Scenic Byway.

byways.review: Catalog lists it only as a state byway; FHWA lists it as a National Scenic Byway (id 68569). The Henry Hudson Drive segment north of Dyckman Hill Road is closed to cars in winter.

byways.name: Pine Barrens Byway
byways.designation: New Jersey Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: About 130 miles in three routes through Burlington, Ocean, Atlantic, Cape May and Cumberland counties, from Batsto and Tuckerton south to Dennisville and Port Elizabeth (CR 542, US 9, CR 559, NJ 50, NJ 49, NJ 47 and others)

facts.fact: Designated a New Jersey Scenic Byway in 2005, formerly called the Southern Pinelands Natural Heritage Trail; about 130 miles of existing roads through five counties and 16 municipalities, administered by the Pinelands Commission, which calls it a National Scenic Byway.

The route runs from Batsto Village in Wharton State Forest, whose furnaces made cannonballs for Washington's army, out to the Tuckerton Seaport, along the edge of the Forsythe National Wildlife Refuge and south past ruins of 18th and 19th century furnaces and glassworks.
Batsto Village lies on CR 542 in Wharton State Forest and is listed on the New Jersey and National Registers of Historic Places.

byways.review: Catalog lists it only as a state byway; FHWA lists it as a National Scenic Byway (FHWA id 81573).

byways.name: Upper Freehold Historic Farmland Scenic Byway
byways.where: Loop of about 24 miles from Allentown through Upper Freehold Township, Monmouth County (CR 539, 524, 526, 27, Red Valley Road, Walnford Road), ending at Walnford Mill

facts.fact: A roughly 24-mile route in Monmouth County around Allentown and Upper Freehold Township, past Historic Walnford, the Old Yellow Meeting House and the hamlet of Imlaystown; many farms have been worked by the same families for generations.
The route crosses Crosswicks Creek on the old iron bridge on Walnford Road and ends where Walnford Road dead-ends at the Walnford Mill.
Walnford is a community on Crosswicks Creek in Upper Freehold Township named for its original owner, Richard Waln.

byways.review: Monmouth County publishes a virtual-tour StoryMap (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/040beb8f56934c018d8e01170ec88a0c) and a 2020 route layer; neither fetched as the official page because the county parks site timed out.

byways.name: Warren Heritage Scenic Byway
byways.where: NJ 57, milepost 2.07 in Greenwich Township to milepost 21.1 in Hackettstown, Warren County, about 19 miles

facts.fact: Route 57 follows the line of an 1806 turnpike between Phillipsburg and Morristown and crosses Scotts, Pohatcong and Point mountains and the valleys of the Musconetcong River and Lopatcong and Pohatcong creeks.

Remnants of the Morris Canal can be seen along the corridor, including a boat basin at Port Murray; a marker in New Village identifies a mile of road built in 1912 of Edison Portland Cement as the first concrete highway in New Jersey.
Route 57 is a 21.1-mile state highway from US 22 in Lopatcong Township to Hackettstown, through mostly farmland and mountains.

byways.name: Western Highlands Scenic Byway
byways.designation: New Jersey Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Sussex County, Hardyston and Vernon townships: CR 515 north from NJ 23, then NJ 94 to the New York line (13-mile spine), plus a 10-mile loop on CR 644, CR 517 and NJ 94 around Vernon

facts.fact: The byway runs north through Hardyston and Vernon townships from Route 23 to the New York border, about 23 miles counting a 13-mile spine and a 10-mile loop, beside the Hamburg Mountain Wildlife Management Area and Wawayanda State Park.

The Appalachian Trail crosses the route north of Vernon, where the Black Creek Indian Site, one of six Native American sites in New Jersey on the historic registers, also lies; resorts along the route offer skiing and golf.
Listed by FHWA as a National Scenic Byway in the northwest corner of the state within the New Jersey Highlands.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. Line exists only in NJDOT's web map featureCollection (see gis.notes), NAME='WESTERN HIGHLANDS'.

issues: FHWA's America's Byways New Jersey page lists six National Scenic Byways: Bayshore Heritage, Delaware River, Millstone Valley, Palisades, Pine Barrens and Western Highlands. The catalog marks only Delaware River and Millstone Valley as national; Bayshore, Palisades and Pine Barrens need the National Scenic Byway designation added. NJDOT's own pages still describe only Delaware River and Millstone Valley as nationally designated (2009), so NJDOT text is out of date on this.

Western Highlands Scenic Byway (state and national) is missing from the catalog. There is no queryable NJDOT line layer; its geometry is only in the featureCollection embedded in NJDOT web map item fed82e3348294996b1a847fc85ef78b5 (NAME='WESTERN HIGHLANDS'), which the integrator would need to read directly rather than via /query.

FHWA per-byway pages (fhwaapps.fhwa.dot.gov/bywaysp/byways/<id>) return HTTP 200 but show a 404 'Page Not Found' body, so they are not used as road URLs. The state page https://fhwaapps.fhwa.dot.gov/bywaysp/States/Show/NJ works.

Several byway organization sites linked from official pages are dead (njscenicbyways.com, which the Pinelands Commission still links). No working Bayshore Heritage byway organization site was found, so NJDOT's page is used.
Millstone Valley length differs within NJDOT's own page (25 vs about 27.5 miles); catalog maps 25 miles.
